transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, thank you for calling S-Net customer billing and accounts. My name is Callum speaking. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Callum, it's Malgorzata calling. I am honestly beside myself this morning because you have charged me twice on my direct debit after upgrading from Fibre 150 to Fibre 500.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You were charged twice on your direct debit after upgrading from Fibre 150 to Fibre 500. Let me open your billing ledger right now. Could you confirm your home address and four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the address is 42 Victoria Crescent, Leeds, LS6 2RJ, and my security PIN is 8104. Because of that double payment, my bank account has gone into an unauthorized overdraft and my electricity bill might bounce!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Malgorzata. I have your account open on my screen now. Let me ask a few specific questions so I can trace both direct debit collections on your ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please look quickly, I barely slept last night when I saw the banking app notification showing two separate withdrawals to S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, looking at your bank statement, what were the exact pound and pence amounts of the two direct debit collections, and on which dates did they leave your bank account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The first payment went out on the 14th of October for £34.20, and then a second payment went out yesterday on the 17th of October for £68.40!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, £34.20 on the 14th of October and £68.40 on the 17th of October. And do both transactions show the exact same S-Net direct debit mandate reference on your statement, or do they have different suffix numbers?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check the transaction details on my banking app... the £34.20 one ends in DD-01, and the £68.40 one ends in DD-02.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That suffix difference is very informative, Malgorzata. Now let me check the date your Fibre 500 upgrade order was placed and the date it went live. Did you place the upgrade online or over the phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I did it over the phone on the 2nd of October when an agent offered me Fibre 500 for £44.00 a month, and the faster speed went live on the 5th of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when you spoke to the sales advisor on the 2nd of October, did they ask for your bank sort code and account number again, or did they tell you it would stay on your existing direct debit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They asked me to read out my sort code and account number to re-confirm the direct debit mandate for the new 24-month contract, which I thought was just a formality.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, and has your bank charged you a daily or fixed unauthorized overdraft fee yet, and if so, what is the exact amount showing on your banking app?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They haven't added a fee yet because I have until 3:30 PM tomorrow to bring the balance back above zero, otherwise my council tax and electricity direct debits will fail.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I have all the figures I need to audit the ledger entries for you, Malgorzata. Let me walk you through what happened on the billing platform between the 2nd and the 17th of October.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please tell me how on earth you took £102.60 in one week when my new package is only supposed to be £44.00 a month!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Here is the exact breakdown. Your normal monthly billing cycle runs from the 1st to the last day of each month, with collection on the 14th.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it has always come out on the 14th of the month for the last three years.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On the 1st of October, before you called to upgrade on the 2nd, your automated October invoice had already been generated at your old Fibre 150 rate of £34.20.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, so the £34.20 on the 14th was the original October bill that was already in the pipeline?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct. Because BACS direct debit files are submitted to the clearing house five working days before the 14th, that £34.20 request under mandate DD-01 was already locked in transit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then why did a second mandate DD-02 take £68.40 three days later on the 17th?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When the sales advisor re-entered your sort code and account number on the 2nd of October, the order system created a brand-new billing sub-account under mandate DD-02 instead of modifying mandate DD-01.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A brand-new sub-account? So the system thought I was taking out a second broadband line?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not a second physical line, Malgorzata, but it failed to link the £34.20 payment already scheduled on DD-01, and instead billed you a full month in advance on Fibre 500 plus pro-rata days without applying your Fibre 150 credit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, let's check the maths on that, because £68.40 doesn't even match £44.00 a month!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me give you the exact penny-by-penny calculation on that £68.40 charge so you can see where every figure came from.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go ahead, I have a pen and paper right here in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: From the 1st of October to the 4th of October is four days on Fibre 150 at £34.20 per month, which works out to £1.10 per day, or £4.41 for those four days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, £4.41 for the first four days of October on Fibre 150. I've written that down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then from the 5th of October, when Fibre 500 went live, to the 31st of October is twenty-seven days at the new £44.00 monthly rate, which works out to £38.32.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, so £4.41 plus £38.32 is £42.73 in total for the whole month of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Spot on—your true net liability for the entire month of October is £42.73. Since you already paid £34.20 on the 14th of October, the only upgrade difference you actually owed for October was £8.53.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Only £8.53! So why did the system take £68.40 on the 17th of October instead of £8.53?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because mandate DD-02 didn't see the £34.20 credit from DD-01, and on top of that it accidentally billed two legacy £34.20 Fibre 150 cycles while migrating the tariff code.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an absolute mess on your billing system's part, Callum. And it has left my current account £55 overdrawn right before my utility bills come out!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me reconcile the two mandates on your account right now so this never happens again. First, I am cancelling duplicate mandate DD-02 and merging the ledger history back under DD-01.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, definitely cancel that duplicate mandate so it doesn't take two payments again in November.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mandate DD-02 is now permanently cancelled. Second, I have applied the £34.20 credit from the 14th of October against the migrated ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about the £68.40 that was wrongfully taken from my bank yesterday? I need that money back in my current account today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Regarding the £68.40 overcollection, I have calculated your exact refund entitlement. Rather than holding the £8.53 October upgrade difference now, I am deferring that £8.53 to your November bill so we can refund the entire £68.40.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, okay, refunding the full £68.40 will definitely clear my overdraft with room to spare. Can you send that £68.40 back to my debit card or via Faster Payments right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On our billing platform, advisors can only trigger instant Faster Payments refunds up to a maximum ceiling of £50.00. Because your refund is £68.40, it has to go through our back-office treasury BACS run.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What?! A back-office BACS run? How long does that take to reach my bank account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A back-office treasury BACS refund requires supervisor sign-off and takes between three and five working days for the funds to clear into your bank account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Three to five working days?! Callum, I just told you my electricity bill and council tax come out tomorrow afternoon and I'm in an unauthorized overdraft right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can we split the £68.40 into two smaller refunds under £50.00 so it goes instantly? Let me check if the system allows split Faster Payments on a single direct debit clawback.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please try splitting it into £34.20 and £34.20 if that gets around the £50 limit!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am testing a split adjustment on invoice INV-904112 now... unfortunately the ledger locks a single direct debit transaction ID to one refund voucher, so the system blocks splitting it below £50.00.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I have to wait three to five working days to get my own money back because your system created a duplicate mandate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait—there is one more route you could use through your bank today, or I can submit the priority BACS refund plus a goodwill credit from here. Let me explain both options clearly, Malgorzata.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What are the two options? I need to know how to stop my bills bouncing tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, under the Direct Debit Indemnity Scheme, your bank can recall an erroneous direct debit collection on the same day if you ring their direct debit team, or second, I can submit the £68.40 priority BACS refund from S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, if I ask my bank to do a Direct Debit Indemnity clawback today, won't S-Net's automated system flag my broadband account as in arrears and cut off my Fibre 500?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a very important point to check. If an indemnity clawback comes in while a BACS refund is also queued, the automated collections engine can put a temporary suspension marker on the sub-account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I definitely cannot risk my broadband getting suspended because I work from home three days a week!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that case, the safest path so your Fibre 500 stays completely uninterrupted is for me to submit the priority BACS refund from here and provide you with an official S-Net error letter for your bank's overdraft team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, let's do the priority BACS refund from your end then, as long as you make sure it doesn't get stuck in a queue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because I am handling your billing case end-to-end, I am submitting the £68.40 BACS refund request under my own queue right now and I will personally monitor the treasury sign-off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, and when will that treasury sign-off happen if you monitor it yourself?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am flagging voucher REF-6840-LDS as urgent hardship priority for the 2:00 PM treasury batch today, which is the fastest internal BACS path we have, clearing in three working days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about if my bank charges me an overdraft fee or bounce fee while I wait those three working days?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To cover any potential bank charges or inconvenience, I am also applying an immediate £25.00 goodwill credit directly to your November S-Net bill right now, which is within my advisor authority.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so £25.00 comes off my November broadband bill, and the £68.40 comes back to my bank account via BACS in three to five working days?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct. Your November bill on the 14th of November will be £44.00 plus the £8.53 October pro-rata balance, minus the £25.00 goodwill credit, making your November collection £27.53.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, £27.53 for November is clear, and I have written down voucher reference REF-6840-LDS for the £68.40 refund.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also generated a formal S-Net Billing Error Confirmation Letter in PDF format and emailed it to your registered email inbox right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What can I use that PDF letter for?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can show or upload that letter to your bank's support chat today—banks routinely grant a temporary fee-free buffer for 72 hours when they see written confirmation of a merchant direct debit error.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I see the email from S-Net Billing with the PDF letter attached now. I will ring my bank as soon as we finish this call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And as promised, Malgorzata, I have put a personal reminder on my desktop for 2:15 PM today to verify that treasury has released voucher REF-6840-LDS to the BACS clearing stream.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will you send me a text message once treasury approves it at 2:15 PM so I at least know it's on the way?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I will send an SMS to your mobile number ending in 409 the moment the treasury batch status changes to Dispatched.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright. I'm still not happy that the £68.40 isn't back in my bank account today, so this won't really be resolved for me until that money actually lands in my account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged all the notes on your account, merged the direct debit mandates under DD-01, applied the £25.00 credit for November, and queued the £68.40 BACS refund.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll look out for your text message after 2:15 PM today and speak to my bank in the meantime.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your Fibre 500 tariff or your November bill breakdown that I can go over for you today, Malgorzata?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the maths on the bill makes sense now, I'm just waiting on the refund to clear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Malgorzata. I will text you the treasury update this afternoon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye, Callum.
